Swiss🇨🇭 1/4/2025 11:09 AM
Swiss prucalopride anecdote Disclaimer: This is all just my personal subjective experience, I did not do any cognitive testing, it was purely my subjective feel. Please also take it as that and not as fact that your experience will be the same it may or may not be. I overall think 5ht4 is a good pathway to target especially due to it's effects on amyloid body production, which is quite a interesting mechanism, the evidence is also there for improvements in cognitive function with oral dosing of 1mg for a few days in healthy people with prucalopride. Background: I am 22 years old, have been using nootropics on off for 3 years. I am generally not depressed or particularly anxious. My attention and top down control is usually pretty good, I don't have ADHD. What I do think I have though is some sort of excessive time daytime sleepiness, mild palmar hyperhidrosis especially in hot temperatures and high stress, slightly elevated blood pressure and mild motivational deficits without noots this in turn may or may not also explain at least partially my anecdotal experience with some of the noots mentioned here. Stimulants I respond well to stimulants such as modafinil. Have not tried methylphenidate or amphetamine. Pemoline feels quite nice for me, in the past i've got great benefits from it, improvements in focus (almost too much), energy and task initiation, my retention and reasoning also seemed to be somewhat improved. Bromantane I am a non-responder it, generally makes me more fatigued and with IN usage seems to give me a cough. Phenylpiracetam - Feels good at high dosages, improvements across the board even in subjective effects like mood and anxiety, overall great if it was more accessible at high dosages I would use it way more.
11:10 AM
Nootropics Tak - I don't respond to well high dossages, make me feel dissociated almost and it becomes hard to hold a train of thought. Lower dosages around 2mg seem to give me subjectively improvements in focus, but not really retention and learning. (I don't really need help with focus) Neboglamine - Felt quite nice, but was a little short lasting and cognitive improvements didn't feel in particular strong (that is with most noots ime). I was in a slightly better mood and it felt like I could learn things better. Piracetam - All around no side effects, feels alright, not particular strong or weak, felt like cognitive improvements accross the board mildly, except focus for me. NSI-189- Felt alright, didn't notice particularly much positive or negative from it over a prolonged period of time. ABT - At high dosages 20mg I get decent long lasting (past it's half life) cognitive improvements. No side effects. Low dosages are negligable for me. Not very cost effective, is even better during it's active half life (which is pretty short). Tropisetron - never used it for a long time only for short amounts of time. Felt like I could focus better maybe? Felt slightly more relaxed. Not sure whether I got any cogntivie improvements from it, if they were present they must have been mild for me. PRL - Felt some improvements in long term retention, but not much that felt like large improvements in short term memory.
11:10 AM
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ The Prucalopride Experience: So as for my past experience with prucalopride. First experience with prucalopride orally. (KW, Prucalopride and BPN)
  • I've used acutely oral prucalopride once at 2 mg iirc with KW and BPN which felt pretty nice, but for some reason as not as strong as Piracetam, KW and BPN. Maybe just my personal response?
I tried both pretty much the next day after the other one. Also as expected I had pretty suvere gastrointestinal distress and diarrhea on when using the 2mg orally with prucalopride, which didn't occur with piracetam and BPN obviously. First experience with prucalopride intranasal. (KW, Prucalopride and BPN) A few days later some anecdotes started comming in about IN prucalopride to mitigate gastrointestinal side effects to which I also started making a nasal spray. My nasal spray could have been made better it wasn't filtered very well and was mildly cloudy, but definitely contained prucalopride. I tested the nasal spray a few days after doing my oral, kw, Puralopride and BPN test. I am not quite sure about the IN dosage anymore, but I think it was around 0.5mg - 0.6mg probably. Personally I didn't notice many outstanding benefits that were different to the oral dosing, it felt like my learning was somewhat improved, but less so my working memory, which comparatively felt more improved on piracetam and BPN maybe I have low PFC cAMP? not sure. Subjectively in terms of mental state, I am not sure what to make of it, it probably did something, but it wasn't very strong for me subjectively to the point that I was like "I fell so much calmer now" or "I feel so much happier now", felt more like a mild boost in hippocampus dependent learning for me. Unfortunately I kept on getting side effects in the gastoinstetinal tract which kept me from using it again at that time. - (edited)
11:11 AM
Pruaclopride Buccal Pouches (Just prucalopride, nothing else) Fast forward a few weeks maybe even months and I notice I still have a lot of prucalpride on me, from when I first tried it. I also still had some empty nic pouches lying around. I thought it may be nice to try some buccal prucalopride for once, as I generally see bucal administration as a more convenient, safe and pleasant drug administration method then IN. I quickly create some prucalopride filled nic pouches. (They were obviously empty and didn't contain any nic) I have to say it felt quite pleasant I wasn't sure how much of it was placebo, but I felt calm and focused with mild noticeable improvements in hippocampal dependent memory. Otherwise no real other changes. Unfortunately also here with this drug administration method I also fairly quickly got unpleasant gastrointestinal side effects. Dosage was likely around 0.8mg iirc. Again unfortunately the side effects were somewhat limiting to the whole thing. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Long Term Prucalopride Orally without side effects (5 weeks) (prucalopride 1-2mg, loperamide 2mg and istra 20-40mg) A few months later @LongTermPotentiation came up with the idea of doing loperamide with prucalopride orally to counteract the side effects. (I know tropi has been used in combination with prucalo to control it's side effects, but I heard it's hard to dose to keep it right and tropi at least mechanistically may counteract some of prucaloprides effects?) I also started hearing from some people like @JC Denton and @SLYMON that it gets a lot better with prolonged use, so seeing that I still had a lot of prucalopride and am going traveling and have less cognitive demanding tasks to do for about 5 weeks I gave it another likely final shot. (edited)
11:12 AM
Day 1: First day it was all about seing whether I can control it's side effects with loperamide to see whether this project would even be sustainable long term. 2mg of loperamide with 1mg of prucalopride and the ball was rolling. Day 2-5: I didn't know what to expect, would I be able to control the side effects or suffer with debilitating diarrhea? Interestingly... It never came. My bowl movements stayed normal when I would be shitting pure water without the loperamide at this point. Things were going well and turned out just as I had hoped. The game was on. So far I didn't feel much of a change in cognition or mood. Week 1-3: In the first week/Days I started feeling more up beat, I wasn't sure, was it related to the prucalopride? or related to the chrismas vibes at uni? doing more with my friends and or that exams were done? Regardless my inhibition was down quite a bit for like 2 days in the beginning, I was quite a bit bolder, layed back and cared much less what people said or thought. I would also say much more what was on my mind. So far I felt quite good about it. Unfortunately, this seemed to fade the longer I used it and my experience seemed to normalize more. I think I had some mild improvements of my cognition above baseline particularly in what felt like my hippocampal dependent memory starting after week 1. My working memory didn't feel very noticeably improved at least subjectively. It felt more like I could remember certain things that people would tell me without having to think about with as much intesnity, but that really was it more or less. Other then that subjectively over weeks 2-3 I felt pretty normal as I would usually, which didn't really bother me tbh, in the end it was an experiment and I was there to see how it would effect me over a long time. I was also on holidays so it was chill in general. (edited)
11:12 AM
  • week 3-5:
Unfortunately it didn't feel like much changed in my experience pretty much the same in terms of what felt like so far in weeks 2-3 with 1mg. Mostly mild improvements in hippocampal dependent memory, but no particular improvements in focus (again my focusing ability is already quite good), energy (no real change here that would have been noticeable outside of the istra that I was running), working memory also didn't feel like it changed particularly noticeable. I reported back to some of you peeps around this time and some of you recommended increasing my oral dosage. So I bit the bullet and increased to 2mg. I ran 2mg from about end of week 3 to week 5. So for approximately almost 2 weeks. I adjusted the loperamide dosage accordingly and side effects still stayed at bay. Over time it felt like my hippocampal dependent memory went from maybe mild improvements to noticeable, but not particularly strong improvements. Again unfortunately no other particular noticeable subjective improvements in mood or anxiety or in other metrics of cognition. Discontinuation period: I am on day 2 now of discontinuing prucalopride. On the first day, I was surprised to be particularly stimulated and almost anxious. My hands were shaking and my voice felt like it was trembling. Was I going through withdrawl? Granted some confounding factors could have been that I was somewhat drunk on new years, but I generally don't get anxious after a drinking (So far I've always felt better the next day after drinking - like a sort of afterglow of being calm and happy and never had any sort of withdrawl even with much higher amounts of alcohol then what I had at that night). Day 2 I feel pretty fine, the anxiety and overstimulation, seems to have died down the the more time has passed and now I feel pretty normal again. (edited)
1
11:12 AM
Overall conclusion TLDR: For me prucalopride over a long time (5 weeks) and at a dosages of 1-2mg orally, was a fun little experiment I learnt quite a few things about how the medication effects me. For me it improved my hippocampal dependent memory, but didn't change much of other cognitive metrics, subject feel wise as mentioned I don't have particular setbacks like depression, anxiety or ADHD so I didn't notice much of a improvement or worsening from my baseline in these parts. I did feel something that could have been classified as withdrawl on the first day of discontinuation, but it also had confounding factors. I am not sure whether I want to give it another try, i've personally had better experiences with other compounds. I was thinking though to give 5ht4 another try if the anecdotes on usmerapride sound good and people like it. I hope this was helpful for some people that may read it.

Swiss🇨🇭
  • week 3-5:
Unfortunately it didn't feel like much changed in my experience pretty much the same in terms of what felt like so far in weeks 2-3 with 1mg. Mostly mild improvements in hippocampal dependent memory, but no particular improvements in focus (again my focusing ability is already quite good), energy (no real change here that would have been noticeable outside of the istra that I was running), working memory also didn't feel like it changed particularly noticeable. I reported back to some of you peeps around this time and some of you recommended increasing my oral dosage. So I bit the bullet and increased to 2mg. I ran 2mg from about end of week 3 to week 5. So for approximately almost 2 weeks. I adjusted the loperamide dosage accordingly and side effects still stayed at bay. Over time it felt like my hippocampal dependent memory went from maybe mild improvements to noticeable, but not particularly strong improvements. Again unfortunately no other particular noticeable subjective improvements in mood or anxiety or in other metrics of cognition. Discontinuation period: I am on day 2 now of discontinuing prucalopride. On the first day, I was surprised to be particularly stimulated and almost anxious. My hands were shaking and my voice felt like it was trembling. Was I going through withdrawl? Granted some confounding factors could have been that I was somewhat drunk on new years, but I generally don't get anxious after a drinking (So far I've always felt better the next day after drinking - like a sort of afterglow of being calm and happy and never had any sort of withdrawl even with much higher amounts of alcohol then what I had at that night). Day 2 I feel pretty fine, the anxiety and overstimulation, seems to have died down the the more time has passed and now I feel pretty normal again. (edited)

Swiss🇨🇭
Overall conclusion TLDR: For me prucalopride over a long time (5 weeks) and at a dosages of 1-2mg orally, was a fun little experiment I learnt quite a few things about how the medication effects me. For me it improved my hippocampal dependent memory, but didn't change much of other cognitive metrics, subject feel wise as mentioned I don't have particular setbacks like depression, anxiety or ADHD so I didn't notice much of a improvement or worsening from my baseline in these parts. I did feel something that could have been classified as withdrawl on the first day of discontinuation, but it also had confounding factors. I am not sure whether I want to give it another try, i've personally had better experiences with other compounds. I was thinking though to give 5ht4 another try if the anecdotes on usmerapride sound good and people like it. I hope this was helpful for some people that may read it.

secretweapon 🌀⚡ 6/19/2025 9:33 PM

Dimethyl Sulfoxide (DMSO) Produces Widespread Apoptosis in the Developing Central Nervous System

DMSO produced widespread apoptosis in the developing mouse brain at all ages tested. Damage was greatest at P7. Significant elevations above the background rate of apoptosis occurred at the lowest dose tested, 0.3 ml/kg.
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2682536/

Unexpected low-dose toxicity of the universal solvent DMSO

Here, we demonstrate that DMSO induces retinal apoptosis in vivo at low concentrations (5 μl intravitreally dosed DMSO in rat from a stock concentration of 1, 2, 4, and 8% v/v) ... Here, we show the mechanism by which low concentrations (2–4% DMSO) induce caspase-3 independent neuronal death that involves apoptosis-inducing factor (AIF) translocation from mitochondria to the nucleus and poly-(ADP-ribose)-polymerase (PARP) activation. These results highlight safety concerns of using low concentrations of DMSO as a solvent for in vivo administration and in biological assays.
https://faseb.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1096/fj.13-235440

Apoptosis in murine lymphoid organs following intraperitoneal administration of dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO)

Taken together, these results showed for the first time that the in vivo administration of DMSO to mice caused apoptosis in lymphoid organs
https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0014480005000900

Dimethyl Sulfoxide (DMSO) Produces Widespread Apoptosis in the Developing Central Nervous System

DMSO produced widespread apoptosis in the developing mouse brain at all ages tested. Damage was greatest at P7. Significant elevations above the background rate of apoptosis occurred at the lowest dose tested, 0.3 ml/kg.
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2682536/

Unexpected low-dose toxicity of the universal solvent DMSO

Here, we demonstrate that DMSO induces retinal apoptosis in vivo at low concentrations (5 μl intravitreally dosed DMSO in rat from a stock concentration of 1, 2, 4, and 8% v/v) ... Here, we show the mechanism by which low concentrations (2–4% DMSO) induce caspase-3 independent neuronal death that involves apoptosis-inducing factor (AIF) translocation from mitochondria to the nucleus and poly-(ADP-ribose)-polymerase (PARP) activation. These results highlight safety concerns of using low concentrations of DMSO as a solvent for in vivo administration and in biological assays.
https://faseb.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1096/fj.13-235440

Apoptosis in murine lymphoid organs following intraperitoneal administration of dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO)

Taken together, these results showed for the first time that the in vivo administration of DMSO to mice caused apoptosis in lymphoid organs

@LongTermPotentiation btw—I only cited these in response to your comment "physiological tissue is way different than in vitro." These studies aren't really my main concern, so let's just assume they could be dismissed with claims about mechanism or dosage. The issue I raised many months ago, which hasn't been addressed, is epigenetic changes. DMSO has a reputation for being safe in the biomedical community because it is assumed to be biologically inert, but that reputation was developed many decades before we had the technology to measure epigenetic impact. The following study concluded that "even at low concentrations (0.1%) DMSO is not inert" and they recommend minimizing DMSO exposure wherever possible. The epigenetic disturbances were so pronounced that the authors cautioned they "may pose a threat."

DMSO induces drastic changes in human cellular processes and epigenetic landscape in vitro

Though clinical trials for medical applications of dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) reported toxicity in the 1960s, later, the FDA classified DMSO in the safest solvent category. DMSO became widely used in many biomedical fields and biological effects were overlooked. Meanwhile, biomedical science has evolved towards sensitive high-throughput techniques and new research areas, including epigenomics and microRNAs. Considering its wide use, especially for cryopreservation and in vitro assays, we evaluated biological effect of DMSO using these technological innovations. We exposed 3D cardiac and hepatic microtissues to medium with or without 0.1% DMSO and analyzed the transcriptome, proteome and DNA methylation profiles. In both tissue types, transcriptome analysis detected >2000 differentially expressed genes affecting similar biological processes, thereby indicating consistent cross-organ actions of DMSO. Furthermore, microRNA analysis revealed large-scale deregulations of cardiac microRNAs and smaller, though still massive, effects in hepatic microtissues. Genome-wide methylation patterns also revealed tissue-specificity. While hepatic microtissues demonstrated non-significant changes, findings from cardiac microtissues suggested disruption of DNA methylation mechanisms leading to genome-wide changes. The extreme changes in microRNAs and alterations in the epigenetic landscape indicate that DMSO is not inert.
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-019-40660-0 The following study found that sub-percent DMSO:
  • slowed both DNA copying in cells (for cell division) and transcription of DNA into RNA (to make proteins). After 24 hours each cell contained ~10-30 % less total DNA + RNA than normal.
  • flipped DNA towards the Z-form, which is a signal that invites an inflammatory interferon (antiviral) response.
  • shifted methyl tags in DNA across thousands of sites, and many of the newly active or silenced genes encode drug-metabolizing enzymes (CYP3A4, CYP2E1, etc.) as well as cell-cycle regulators. # Low dose dimethyl sulfoxide driven gross molecular changes have the potential to interfere with various cellular processes
There are several reports demonstrating that even at very low concentrations (0.05–2.5%, v/v), DMSO can affect gene expression[43][44][45][46][47][48][49][50]
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-018-33234-z TL;DR: DMSO is not inert. It reshapes DNA architecture, turns genes on and off, and affects methylation patterns in ways that scientists are just beginning to understand. Over time, repeated exposure leads to a hardening of epigenetic and pharmacokinetic changes. Oh, and be very afraid!! (Almost forgot to throw in a little fear mongering) Boo!
